h: פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תָבוֹא, ד׳ Ki Savo, 4
Bikkurim and Shabbos Bind the Soul to Its Root

p: "Whoever brings a gift to a talmid chacham
is as though he offered Bikkurim."
is in the aspect of a talmid chacham,
and it is hinted in the Gemara (Shabbos 119a):
"Are you more important to us than she?"
than the meal of a talmid chacham;
and surely it has a connection
For the matter of bringing the Bikkurim
that then there shines in his heart
the root and source of the growths,
"the first of the fruit of the ground,"
to bring them to the House of Hashem.
to the root, to Hashem Yisbarach,
"and you shall bow down before Hashem your God";
is with outstretched hands and feet,
meaning the nullification of all his faculties
above the grasp of human intellect;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹטָה כא, ב)
as they said, of blessed memory (Sotah 21b),
"And wisdom — from Ayin is it found":
in one who makes himself as nothing,
And through this he can reach
the aspect of the existence of wisdom
Now this is the root of
the aspect of the holiness of the Kohen in the soul,
"For the lips of the Kohen shall guard knowledge";
and Daas is the inwardness of Keser,
as Rashi, of blessed memory, explains (Ki Sisa, Shemos 31:3):
only it flows to him from the root.
And therefore the Kohanim were chosen
כִּי רַק עַל יָדָם יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת
for only through them can there be
And this too is the aspect
of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
therefore it was said to him (Bereishis 12:2):
in all the souls of Yisrael too
one can reach through his deeds
those are threefold in a single third,
But in truth here too the meaning is
are included in all the souls of Yisrael;
there are the souls of the Kohanim,
who are from the root of the aspect
of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
And the Levi'im are of the aspect of
Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
"and I gave them to him for fear, and he feared Me."
And the Yisraelim are of the aspect of
Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
and there was included in him
the aspect of both of them;
for the aspect of Avraham and Yitzchak alone,
being from the side of service,
through a lack of service in the soul,
as there came forth from them
Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
the root of holiness without measure,
"and you shall spread out to the west and to the east," etc.
And let us return to the matter:
that the one who brings the Bikkurim
from the aspect of the holiness of a Kohen,
at the beginning of reciting the passage:
he has not yet declared anything,
so what is the expression "I declare"?
But it is in the manner of
there is no speech and there are no words," etc.;
for there is declaring without speech,
the aspect of the hint of wisdom.
there sparkles in him the hint
of the aspect of the holiness of the Kohen;
and this is why he says "to Hashem your God,"
that is, to the aspect of his holiness.
"that I have come to the land
which Hashem swore to our fathers
Only according to what was said above:
to Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
to give to him and his seed
in every first of the good growth,
of the power of the Giver.
אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (בְּרֵאשִׁית טו, ח)
Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him (Bereishis 15:8):
"By what shall I know that I shall inherit it?"
that is, that there be in this permanence
that they not be sunk, Heaven forbid,
in the matters of This World,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִהְיֶה נִשְׁכָּח מֵהֶם
and through this there be forgotten from them
the land would vomit them out.
And for this there made with him
that there be permanence for his seed after him,
that they would never be cut off
from the root of this holiness.
And this is why he mentions the oath,
for by this power he comes
to the aspect of bringing Bikkurim,
so that the root shines in him,

p: And on the day of Shabbos
there shines in the souls of Yisrael too
at the second meal, that of the Holy Ancient One,
שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
which corresponds to Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
through the nullification of all the faculties
Yisrael are endeared before the Omnipresent:
and in the merit of tithes," etc.;
'And you shall rejoice in all the good,' etc."
as the Tanchuma (on this parsha) expounds
from the aspect of the shining of the root.
And therefore it says at the end of the passage:
"And you shall rejoice in all the good";
for from this joy grows in the heart,
when the root shines from the source.
And as they said, of blessed memory (Berachos 30b),
that he said, about his being very joyful:
and through this he is in joy,
above the faculties of the mind,
and from this joy is born in the heart.
And so they said in Shabbos (88a)
that He will in the future restore them,
"the joy that is from of old," etc.;
for from cleaving to the root,
which is the shining of the root,
we say "They shall rejoice in Your kingship"
"And you shall rejoice in your festival."
